criteria.any_code_fail_later: Three uppercase letters always form a currency value; report an error only when money construction or arithmetic first requires the missing scale.
criteria.any_code_scale_two: Three uppercase letters always form a currency value; unknown codes quietly assume 2 minor-unit digits.
criteria.pinned_members: Only members of the version-pinned ISO 4217 table, with their pinned scales, form currency values; anything else is rejected where checked.

admit_currency.instructions: Given the verified excerpts, which admission rule for currency values is most consistent?

criteria.equality_open_ordering_closed: == and != decide mismatched currencies as unequal; <, <=, > and >= fail on mismatched currencies.
criteria.minor_disregarding_unit: Every comparison operator weighs minor units alone and disregards currency.
criteria.mismatch_always_errors: ==, != and all ordering operators fail whenever currencies differ.

compare_money.instructions: Given the verified excerpts, which mixed-currency comparison behavior is most consistent?

criteria.fixed_width: All decimals are written with a decimal point followed by exactly 18 digits.
criteria.stored_form: The encoding keeps whatever scale the value was stored with, so equal values may encode differently.
criteria.trimmed_form: Fractional trailing zeros are removed, integral values omit the point, and negative zero is written 0, giving one encoding per value.

encode_decimal.instructions: Given the verified excerpts, which decimal wire encoding is most consistent?

state: Three CanLang value-semantics details need rulings grounded strictly in the attached verified excerpts. First, decimal values cross the MCP boundary as canonical decimal strings: decide the exact canonical text form. Second, currency is an ISO code and money rounds to the currency's pinned minor-unit scale: decide whether codes outside the pinned table are values at all, and if so what scale they carry. Third, money of unlike currencies must remain groupable but never ordered or summed: decide what == and the ordering operators do when currencies differ.
